chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali from Uthman ibn Ahmad al-Sammak from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Hashmi from al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl al-Busrai from Saad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Ansari from Abd Allah ibn Ziyad al-Yamani from Ikrimah ibn Ammar from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talha from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'We, the children of Abd al-Muttalib, are the chiefs of the people of Paradise: I am Ali, Hamza, Ja'far, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and al-Mahdi.'

key_terms.بَنُو عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ: Children of Abd al-Muttalib (the Prophet's clan)
key_terms.سَادَةُ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ: Chiefs/leaders of the people of Paradise

ai.seo_question: Who are the chiefs of Paradise according to the Prophet's statement in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tusi's *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the 'Six Imams' (al-A'imma al-Sittah) as the core of the Banu Abd al-Muttalib's spiritual authority, explicitly including Imam al-Mahdi to affirm his continuity within the Ahl al-Bayt. By listing Mahdi alongside the Prophet and the four earlier Imams, it underscores the Shia doctrine of the Imamate's divine designation and the eschatological role of the twelfth Imam as the ultimate leader of Paradise.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 142 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Ali from Uthman bin Ahmad Sammak from Ibrahim bin Abdullah Hashmi from Hasan bin Fadhl Busrai from Saad Ibn Abdul Hamid Ansari from Abdullah bin Ziyad Yamami from Akrama bin Ammar from Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talha from Anas bin Malik that he said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: “We, the children of Abdul Muttalib are the chiefs of Paradise dwellers; that is I, Ali, Hamza (chief of the martyrs), Ja’far with two wings, Hasan, Husain, and the Mahdi.”
